title: AI accelerator ships confidential-inference tier with attestation by H1 2027
body: A purpose-built AI inference accelerator will ship or be unveiled with confidential computing as a named, load-bearing feature of the part itself — on-die root-of-trust, TEE-I/O so the model weights and activations stay encrypted in use across the CPU-accelerator boundary, and signed-model attestation that lets a tenant cryptographically verify which weights are running before sending data — marketed as a named confidential-inference SKU or managed tier by H1 2027. The June 24 OpenAI-Broadcom Jalapeno unveiling proved that buyer-designed rack-scale inference silicon is now real, but it disclosed no security-silicon angle, leaving an explicit gap: the inference accelerator wave so far competes on performance-per-watt and fabric bandwidth, not on confidentiality of the model and the prompt. Two structural forces close that gap. First, the same regulated and sovereign buyers driving custom-silicon economics also carry the heaviest data-residency and IP-protection requirements, and merchant accelerators already carry the primitives (NVIDIA Confidential Computing on Hopper/Blackwell, AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX with TEE-I/O) waiting to be productized into a named inference tier rather than a developer-preview flag. Second, the agentic-AI security cycle keeps tying risk to model-supply-chain integrity (poisoned checkpoints, unauthenticated registries), and signed-model attestation is the hardware-rooted answer to 'prove the weights I am querying are the weights I approved.' The falsifiable core is a NAMED part or managed tier where confidential inference — encrypted-in-use weights plus tenant-verifiable attestation — is the marketed feature, disclosed at a venue such as AMD Advancing AI (July 22-23), Hot Chips (August 23-25), Black Hat (August), or a hyperscaler launch. What does NOT count: a generic 'we support confidential computing' line on a GPU spec sheet with no inference-specific tier; a research paper or preprint with no shipping part; a confidential-VM offering that merely runs an unmodified accelerator without TEE-I/O or model attestation; or a restatement of an existing developer-preview that was already announced before today.

reasoning.given: Regulated and sovereign inference buyers need encrypted-in-use weights and tenant-verifiable model attestation
reasoning.so_that: A vendor productizes TEE-I/O plus signed-model attestation into a named confidential-inference SKU or managed tier
reasoning.landing: Named confidential-inference accelerator tier with signed-model attestation ships by H1 2027
reasoning.plain_language: AI chips will soon offer a mode that keeps the model and your data secret and lets you check which model is really running.

summary: The June 24 Jalapeno unveiling proved buyer-designed inference silicon is real but disclosed no security angle. Because regulated and sovereign buyers need encrypted-in-use weights and verifiable model attestation, expect an AI accelerator to ship a named confidential-inference tier with TEE-I/O and signed-model attestation by H1 2027, distinct from a generic confidential-computing checkbox.
